text:
sre-bot: INCIDENT: cont-batch streaming latency spike detected in prod-usw2. p95 stepped from ~120ms -> 420ms, p99 jumped to ~2.6s. Route: /v1/stream. Paging oncall now. Auto-alert: cont-batch-queue-depth > 95th percentile, scheduling fairness metric degraded.

Ken: I'm oncall, looking at dashboards. Any customer-facing errors?

Ana: support: two customers reporting streaming stalls and reconnects (TICKET-1881, TICKET-1883). No 5xxs in frontend, but client reconnect frequency up.

Lisa: From infra view I'm seeing long-lived batches forming on the continuous batching path. Mixed sequence length distribution spiked (many short + a few very long). That causes batch packing to block shorter requests behind long ones; scheduler fairness counters show preemption lag. KV cache evictions also increased.

Ken: good, that matches the trace spans I'm pulling. Streaming send stalls align with large KV lookups around model kv-evict cycles. Stack traces point to cont-batcher wait queue.

Michael: ML note: model variant rtx-q8_512 shows increased step time when seqlen > 6k, quantized fallback paths probably being triggered for those long requests. Might be spilling to CPU for attention ops.

Lisa: Proposed mitigations (fast):
- reduce max_batch_size from 32 -> 8 for cont-batchers serving streaming routes
- enable strict mixed-seqlen shedding for requests with seqlen > 2000 (route-level circuit)
- turn on scheduler fairness weighting (shorter request priority)
- temporarily route streaming to single-request streaming allocator (latency-optimized) if p99 > 1s

Ken: Can you apply the first two? I'll coordinate with routing to divert streaming to the latency allocator as a fallback.

Lisa: Applying config now. Patch: ```
PATCH /api/v1/configs/cont-batch
{
  "max_batch_size": 8,
  "mixed_seqlen_shedding": { "enabled": true, "threshold_tokens": 2000 },
  "fairness_mode": "short-first"
}
```

Lisa: config rollout started -> nodes in us-west-2 are receiving. Expect steady-state within ~45s per pool.

sre-bot: Deploy job started (deploy-7921), progress updates will follow.

Ken: I'll kick routing fallback if we still see p99 > 1s after config. Monitoring panels refreshed.

(60s later)

Lisa: Observability: queue depth dropping 40%, p95 back to ~180ms, p99 down to ~720ms but still above SLO on a few hosts. KV evictions down ~30%.

Ana: Support: customers updated. One customer reports improvement, second still seeing occasional recon, asking for ETA.

Michael: Re: model paths — I'm enabling a temporary per-request quantization tolerance to avoid slow fallback for huge seqlen. This will reduce long-run accuracy slightly but should avoid CPU fallback. Applying on model proxy.

Ken: Good. If fallback not enough, route-specific throttling for extremely long sessions (>=6000 tokens) may be needed.

(180s later)

Lisa: p99 now ~420ms across the cluster, streaming stalls no longer appearing in traces. Scheduler fairness counters show short-first throughput increased. Reduced overall GPU efficiency by ~6% but tail improved.

Ken: Paging: cancel initial page for oncall rotation. I'll stay until Ron takes handoff. @Ron can you take monitoring for next 30m?

Ron: Taking handoff — watching p95/p99 and reconnect rate for 30m. If p99 stabilizes under 600ms and reconnects < 0.1% we'll close incident.

Ken: Handoff notes:
- config changes: max_batch_size=8, mixed_seqlen_shedding=true, fairness=short-first
- temporary model proxy quant tolerance enabled for long-seq requests
- routing fallback enabled if p99 > 1s: `route-allocator:latency-opt`
- impacted customers: TICKET-1881 (monitoring OK), TICKET-1883 (follow-up with support)

Ron: ack. I'll escalate to infra if p99 creeps above 900ms again. Adding runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/cont-batch-tail

Ana: Support will follow up with the remaining affected customer and set expectation for a postmortem if they request.

Ken: Logging for postmortem: collect heap snapshots and cont-batcher histograms from the 3 hosts that had worst p99 (host-34, host-41, host-52). Also export traces for 10% of streaming requests in the window [2412345600 - 2412346000].

Lisa: grabbing artifacts now and uploading to the incident s3 bucket.

(10m later)

Ron: p99 steady ~380ms, reconnects ~0.02%. Closing action: keep short-first fairness for 24h and revisit batcher sizing with ML for model-variant sequence patterns.

Ken: Great work. I'll schedule follow-up with ML + infra to tune batch sizes and evaluate per-tenant qps shaping.

sre-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: cont-batch streaming latency spike mitigated. Root cause: mixed sequence length packing + large-seq model fallback triggering CPU paths + temporarily degraded scheduler fairness. Remediation: batch size reduction, short-first scheduling, quantization tolerance, routing fallback. Postmortem owner: Lisa.

(Reaction: :thumbsup: from Ken, Ron, Ana)
